sql:
SELECT COUNT(p.p_promo_sk) AS promo_rows, COUNT(1) AS n
FROM   TPCDS_DB.store_sales ss
LEFT JOIN TPCDS_DB.promotion p ON ss.ss_promo_sk = p.p_promo_sk AND p.p_channel_tv = 'N'
WHERE  ss.ss_customer_sk IS NULL

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query spends most of its time scanning the store_sales table and applying the IS NULL filter on ss_customer_sk, which likely reads a large fraction of the table because the filter is not highly selective. The subsequent broadcast join with the tiny promotion table and the two-phase aggregation are comparatively lightweight.

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join tpcds_db.promotion p on … and p.p_channel_tv = ')
The store_sales scan reads many rows because the predicate ss_customer_sk IS NULL has low selectivity; partitioning or indexing on ss_customer_sk could reduce I/O.

The left outer join with a filter on the build side (p_channel_tv='N') may prevent join reordering or predicate pushdown that could otherwise reduce the probe side earlier, but the promotion table is already filtered before the join.
The final single-partition shuffle for aggregation could become a bottleneck if the number of partial aggregation partitions is very large, though each partition only emits two counters.
